ns2:section.sectionText: Database Administration & Scaling for IS. Prerequisite: IS 455 - Database Design & Prototyping, or IS 206 Database Concepts & Application. Involves database administration (DBA) broadly relevant to computational information science work…Involves database administration (DBA) broadly relevant to computational information science work. Explores several types of scalable database engines, using popular NOSQL and SQL products. Develops practical skills for managing reliable DBMS for production systems or to create analytically-focused NOSQL derivatives. Small student teams will experiment and present findings to the class, with student-directed inquiry encouraged. Readings, discussions, and situational problems drawn from real scenarios will involve managerial, ethical, and other aspects of the human side of professional DBA work. Some intro to virtual machines and cloud systems administration is included. Restricted to Information Sciences undergraduate majors until 1/14/22 by noon. For more information about this major, please visit: http://go.ischool.illinois.edu/BSIS. We will not provide overrides, please wait until the course restrictions are removed. Questions may be sent to bsis-advising@illinois.edu.
ns2:section.sectionNotes: Not intended for students with Freshman or Sophomore class standing. Restricted to Undergrad - Urbana-Champaign.
